Nombres: es: Camino Aragonés, en: Aragonese Way, eu: Aragoiko bidea
Descripcion: The Camino Aragonés begins at the Spanish-French border and joins the Camino Francés in Navarre.
Descripcion En: The Camino Aragonés begins at the Spanish-French border and joins the Camino Francés in Navarre.

Nombres: ga: Camino Fisterra, es: Camino Finisterre
Descripcion: The Camino Fisterra leaves Santiago de Compostella and heads West, to Fisterra/Finisterre, the End of the World. This Camino is often undertaken by pilgrims who have arrived at Santiago de Compostella by other routes and wish to continue to the Westernmost part of Spain.
Descripcion En: The Camino Fisterra leaves Santiago de Compostella and heads West, to Fisterra/Finisterre, the End of the World. This Camino is often undertaken by pilgrims who have arrived at Santiago de Compostella by other routes and wish to continue to the Westernmost part of Spain.

Nombres: ga: Camiño francés, fr: Camino Frances, en: French Way, es: Camino francés, eu: Frantses bidea
Descripcion: El Camino Francês es la ruta mas popular, viniendo de Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port France a Santiago de Compostella.
Descripcion En: The Camino Frances is the most popular Camino route, running from Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port in France to Santiago de Compostella.

Nombres: es: Camino Ingles, en: English Way
Descripcion: The Camino Ingles is a short camino from Ferrol or A Coruña on the Northen coast of Spain. The route was traditionally used by pilgrims from Northern Europe.
Descripcion En: The Camino Ingles is a short camino from Ferrol or A Coruña on the Northen coast of Spain. The route was traditionally used by pilgrims from Northern Europe.

Nombres: es: Camino Invierno, en: Winter Way
Descripcion: The Camino Invierno (Winter Way) is a Camino that runs from Ponferrada to Santiago de Compostella, somewhat to the South of the French Way. It then joins the Camino Sanabrés and approaches Santiago de Compostella from the South. Traditionally, pilgrims used this way to avoid the snows of O Cebreiro in wintertime, from which its name derives.
Descripcion En: The Camino Invierno (Winter Way) is a Camino that runs from Ponferrada to Santiago de Compostella, somewhat to the South of the French Way. It then joins the Camino Sanabrés and approaches Santiago de Compostella from the South. Nombres: es: Camino Madrid, en: Camino Madrid
Descripcion: The Camino Madrid begins at the Plazuela de Santigo in Madrid and joins the Camino Francés at Sahagún.
Descripcion En: The Camino Madrid begins at the Plazuela de Santigo in Madrid and joins the Camino Francés at Sahagún.

Nombres: es: Camino del Norte, en: Northern Way
Descripcion: The Camino del Norte follows the Northen coastline of Spain. This route follows the Via Agrippa for some of its way, which was used in the Middle Ages by Christian pilgrims when travel along the French Way was dangerous.
Descripcion En: The Camino del Norte follows the Northen coastline of Spain. This route follows the Via Agrippa for some of its way, which was used in the Middle Ages by Christian pilgrims when travel along the French Way was dangerous.

Nombres: pt: Caminho Português, es: Camino Portugués, en: Portuguese Way
Descripcion: The Caminho Português (Camino Portuguese) covers the Camino routes starting in Portugal, usually Lisbon or Porto. Short pilgrimages usually start in Tui in Spain, It is the second-most popular route, after the French route. Variants include the side-pilgrimage to Fátima, the coastal route and the Spiritual Variant.
Descripcion En: The Caminho Português (Camino Portuguese) covers the Camino routes starting in Portugal, usually Lisbon or Porto. Variants include the side-pilgrimage to Fátima, the coastal route and the Spiritual Variant.

Descripcion: The Camino Primitivo, or Original Camino is the oldest of the Camino routes to Santiago de Compostella. King Alfosno II of Asturias is considered its first pilgrim in the 9th century.
Descripcion En: The Camino Primitivo, or Original Camino is the oldest of the Camino routes to Santiago de Compostella. King Alfosno II of Asturias is considered its first pilgrim in the 9th century.

Descripcion: The Camino Sanabrés starts in Granja de Moreruela and follows the royal road between Meseta and Galacia, reaching Santiago de Compostella from the South. It is often used by pilgrims on the Vía de la Plata as a final stage to Santiago de Compostella. The route is less tavelled than the major caminos and has a reputation for being peaceful and gentle.

Nombres: es: Vía de la Plata, en: Silver Way, en: Mozarabic Way
Descripcion: The Vía de la Plata (Silver Way) is a Camino that runs from Seville and runs through the whole of Western Spain to Santiago de Compostella. The camino itself runs from Seville and joins either the French Camino at Astorga on the Camino Sanabrés at Granja de la Moreruela. The route has been used for commerce and pilgrimage since ancient times. Despite the name, "Plata" comes from the Arabic word al-balat or paved road and refers to the original Roman road.
